text.p: ITT Industries Inc will become the world's largest pump manufacturer with the pricey purchase of Goulds Pumps Inc, a deal some on Wall Street say saved Goulds from a hostile takeveover.
"This acquisition catapults us to a solid number one in the world from number two," said Travis Engen, chairman of White Plains, N.Y.-based ITT Industries, in an interview.

He declined to comment specifically on whether his company acted as Goulds' "white knight," though he said a poison pill adopted by Goulds as part of the deal gives the target "the opportunity to be in more control in the next few months."
A Goulds spokeswoman said ITT Industries made the initial approach for the deal and declined to comment further.
Early Monday, ITT Industries said it agreed to acquire Goulds for $37 a share, or approximately $815 million in cash, plus the assumption of $119 million of Goulds' debt.

Speculation that ITT Industries was a friendly alternative to a hostile bid for Goulds was driven by Goulds saying minutes after the deal was announced that it had adopted a shareholder rights plan, arbitrageurs said.

"That is atypical but not unheard of," said an arbitrageur. "It seems Goulds has been shopped around for several years. The price seems rich, so maybe there was someone else, amid some aggressive bidding."
Engen said ITT Industries' fluid technology unit posted revenues of $1.3 billion last year, while Goulds' revenues were $775 million.
Combined, Goulds and ITT Industries' fluid technology will have about $2.1 billion in annual revenue, topping Japan-based Ebara Corp's $1.6 billion in annual fluid technology revenues, Engen said
He estimated the overall global pump business to be worth about $15 billion annually.

Thomas Burns, analyst with NatWest Securities, said, "It seemed to me that they (ITT Industries) had a breadth of product, but not a lot of depth. This gives them depth and solidifies their pump business. It looks like a rather full price to me; I don't think anyone is going to compete against them with this deal."
"If were the CFO of Goulds, I would go home and pour myself a glass of Scotch. They got a great price," Burns added.
